keyProps.BaseUIComponentProps<ElementType, State,: Omit<WithBaseUIEvent<ComponentPropsWithRef<ElementType>>, 'className'|'color'|'defaultValue'|'defaultChecked'|'style'> & { className?: string | ((state: State) => string | undefined); style?: CSSProperties | ((state: State) => CSSProperties | undefined); render?: ReactElement | ComponentRenderFn<RenderFunctionProps, State> }. NOTE: native `color`, `defaultValue` and `defaultChecked` are REMOVED and re-declared by each component.
keyProps.NativeButtonProps: { nativeButton?: boolean } @default true — 'whether the component renders a native <button> when replaced via render'.
keyProps.NonNativeButtonProps: { nativeButton?: boolean } @default false — used by parts that are not buttons by default.
keyProps.WithBaseUIEvent<T>: Maps every event handler prop to receive a BaseUIEvent, adding preventBaseUIHandler.
keyProps.BaseUIEvent<E>: E & { preventBaseUIHandler(): void; readonly baseUIHandlerPrevented?: boolean }
keyProps.ComponentRenderFn<Props, State>: (props: Props, state: State) => ReactElement<unknown> — the render callback type.

dataAttributes: Not applicable — this record defines the shared prop contract through which every part receives state and emits data-* attributes.
renderProp: BaseUIComponentProps is the reason every part is uniform: className/style accept state-function form, render accepts element-or-function, and all event handlers are wrapped so consumers can call event.preventBaseUIHandler(). When migrating a React Aria component's props type, `Omit<AriaXProps, ...> & BaseUIComponentProps<'div', State>` is the idiomatic target.
controlled: Not a component; the controlled convention (value/defaultValue/onValueChange + ChangeEventDetails) is defined in internals/createBaseUIEventDetails and restated per component.
formIntegration: Native `name`/`value` submission is a per-component concern; Base UI removes the native `defaultValue`/`defaultChecked` from the shared props so each component can define its own controlled/uncontrolled pair.
notableDifferences: `is*` prop naming is gone: RAC's isDisabled/isSelected/isOpen/isReadOnly become disabled/selected/open/readOnly in Base UI (with a few documented exceptions such as Menu's `open`), so a mechanical rename is required and TypeScript will flag every site.
RAC passes hover/press/focus-visible state into className callbacks; Base UI state objects are deliberately minimal (see tabs record) — interaction states belong in CSS.
